clue.text: Behind barrier, little time to go over it

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece going over another sits above it, so the time comes first

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a railing is a fence or barrier

explanation.surface: Someone stuck behind a barrier has only a moment to climb over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go over it' places T above RAILING in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something trailing lags behind the rest.

clue.text: One perhaps eyed second dessert

parts.note: pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a second helping of dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyed' reads as 'looked at' but means 'having eyes': a potato has eyes, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example. PUD is British slang for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a potato is a vegetable with eyes, the buds on its skin.

clue.text: Cutting reserves, a mistake

indicators.note: cutting means each word is docked of its final letter

parts.note: to book is to reserve, and the plural gives two of them

explanation.surface: Slashing the reserve funds turned out to be an error.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'reserves' supplies BOOK twice; 'Cutting' docks the K from each.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a boo-boo is an informal word for a silly blunder or slip.

clue.text: Distance across doorstep, perhaps, that's halved

parts.note: a doorstep is British slang for a very thick slice of bread, one example of it

indicators.note: halved keeps only the front half of the word that

explanation.surface: Someone measures a doorstep and finds it is half the size expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halved' keeps TH, the first half of 'that'. A doorstep in Britain is also a thick slice of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: width, the measurement from one side to the other.

clue.text: Bet party gets seat

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it
a side is one party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: A gambler's wager wins someone a seat at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: seat is a polite word for the buttocks.

clue.text: Unspecified number, crime in the Spanish capital going up, never going down?

indicators.note: in places the number and crime inside the turned-round capital
going up in a down entry means the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
Baku is the capital of Azerbaijan
N stands for an unspecified number in maths
a sin is a wrongdoing or crime

explanation.surface: Crime in a Spanish capital is on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Baku is the capital of Azerbaijan. 'going up' reverses the Spanish article and capital together, and 'in' slots the number and crime in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a ship that cannot be sunk never goes under, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Bloke captures Aussie native in desert

indicators.note: captures means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a man is a bloke
a roo, short for kangaroo, is native to Australia

explanation.surface: A man catches a kangaroo out in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a noun of sand; it is the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to maroon someone is to abandon them somewhere isolated.

clue.text: Type of 25 cross, not entirely rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the pair of words is thrown back, read in reverse

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix
something that is not entirely so is only in part so

explanation.surface: A puzzle with a cross reference that is only partly turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is SPIDER. 'rejected' reverses ROOD PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the trapdoor is a spider that ambushes prey from a hinged burrow lid.

clue.text: Scrub over a regular report

indicators.note: over means the first word is laid over and around the second

parts.note: to scrub a plan is to cancel or annul it

explanation.surface: Someone cleans up a routine report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrub' suggests cleaning but means cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a company's yearly report is called its annual, published at regular intervals.

clue.text: Time that flies

definitions.meaning: slang for a prison sentence, from birdlime, rhyming slang for time
a creature with wings that flies

explanation.surface: Time flies, as the saying goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: prison time in slang, and a flying creature.

clue.text: East End houses don't have the credentials to accommodate white 25

indicators.note: houses means the district holds the rest inside it

parts.note: Bow is a district in London's East End

indicators.note: accommodate means the two words take the colour in among them

parts.note: to lack is to not have
ID, identification, is a person's credentials

explanation.surface: East End houses lack the paperwork to take in a white spider.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of London's East End. 'to accommodate' puts W in the middle of the lacking and ID pieces, and 'houses' sets that inside the district. 25 is SPIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the black widow is a venomous spider.

clue.text: Disaster — "failure" is another synonym, completely obvious for starters

indicators.note: for starters means the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A thesaurus note: failure is another obvious synonym for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' takes the first letters of 'failure is another synonym completely obvious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a humiliating total failure or catastrophe.

clue.text: 25 that can jump — rating one degree

parts.note: a rating is a sailor, and so is an old salt
I is the Roman numeral one
a grade is a degree or level

explanation.surface: A rating scale gives each jump a degree of difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' reads as a score but is a sailor, SALT. 25 is SPIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: saltigrade spiders, the jumping spiders, move by leaping.

clue.text: Fine man for philosophy

parts.note: a fine thread is thin
a king is a piece, or man, in chess

explanation.surface: A fine man is suited to philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is a chess piece, here the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a philosophy is a way of thought or reasoning.

clue.text: Eternal fool poked by stick with malice in the end

indicators.note: poked by means the fool is pierced with the other pieces inside

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to gel is to stick or set

indicators.note: in the end means the final letter of malice is taken

explanation.surface: A fool is jabbed with a stick out of malice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' is the verb GEL, not a cane; 'in the end' gives E from malice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that never ages lasts forever.

clue.text: Model son to give father a thrashing? That's about right!

parts.note: to tan someone is to give them a thrashing

indicators.note: about means the father goes around the letter for right

parts.note: dad is father

explanation.surface: A son tells of thrashing his dad and claims it was fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give father a thrashing' is TAN DAD, with 'about' putting R in DAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a standard is a model or benchmark to copy.

clue.text: 25, left defender?

parts.note: red stands for the political left
a back is a defender in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A left-sided defender on the football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is SPIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the redback is a venomous Australian spider.

clue.text: Scoundrel I summon up in US car

parts.note: a cad is a scoundrel

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to call is to summon

explanation.surface: A rogue confesses to calling for an American car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses CALL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Cadillac is an American make of luxury car.

clue.text: Lift tool, say, the axe

parts.note: to heave is to lift

indicators.note: say signals that the garden tool's name is spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: a hoe is a garden tool

explanation.surface: Lift your tool, the axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the axe' is no tool here: it means dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: getting the heave-ho, like getting the axe, means being sacked or dumped.

clue.text: Start reviewing it with caveat

indicators.note: reviewing suggests going over the words again in a new order

explanation.surface: A start on reviewing it, with a caveat attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewing' rearranges IT and CAVEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to start a machine is to set it going.

clue.text: Keen to bury leak, head-er deleted as sinister

indicators.note: to bury means the cry surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry

indicators.note: head-er deleted, a pun on header, means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to seep is to leak

explanation.surface: A mourner hopes to hush up a sinister leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head-er deleted' drops S from SEEP to give EEP; 'to bury' puts that in CRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something sinister is unsettling and eerie.

clue.text: In goal, attempt catches

indicators.note: catches means the attempt holds the goal inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A shot at goal that gets caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the definition: fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: when something is in, it is fashionable.

clue.text: Bottom disappearing, the king is upon one!

definitions.text: Bottom disappearing, the king is upon one!

indicators.note: is upon means the king letter sits above the word one in this down entry
in a down entry the bottom letter of the word is the last, which goes

parts.note: R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A king sits on his seat, his bottom vanishing into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom disappearing' drops the final E of 'the' (the bottom, in a down entry); 'is upon' stacks R over 'one'. The whole clue pictures a monarch seated, or anyone on the loo.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's chair of state, and slang for a toilet: either way, where a king sits.

clue.text: One going down for a long time, a reviled criminal in prison, is on for release

definitions.text: One going down for a long time

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the shortened jail
for release means those words are let out of prison
criminal suggests the letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A villain gets a long sentence and is up for release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges A REVILED; 'for release' lets IS ON out of the jail word, leaving PR; 'in' puts the shuffle inside. 'going down' is diving, not jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a diver goes down underwater, holding their breath a long time to bring up oysters.

clue.text: A type of 25 in ebbing stream

indicators.note: ebbing means the stream runs back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a flow is a stream

explanation.surface: A spider caught in a receding stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is SPIDER. 'ebbing' reverses FLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the wolf spider is a hunting spider that chases its prey.

clue.text: Innermost part of bowel remains clean

indicators.note: innermost part means the central letter of bowel is taken

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Clearing out the bowel's inner contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to wash something is to clean it.

clue.text: Do what you do endlessly, 17? That's you!

definitions.text: Do what you do endlessly, 17? That's you!

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut from the word

parts.note: the creature addressed spins webs, so what it does is spin
17 across is REDBACK, read as an instruction: RED back, giving its letters reversed

explanation.surface: Someone urges a 17 to keep doing what it does, recognising it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts SPIN to SPI; 17, REDBACK, is read as RED back, giving DER. The whole clue addresses a web-spinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A web-spinning arachnid, of which the redback at 17 is one kind.

clue.text: 25 hasn't uncoiled, moth initially trapped

indicators.note: trapped means the shuffled letters close around the moth's letter
this word means the letters it governs are mixed up, so they are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the fodder is the word hasn't plus the un that opens uncoiled, a split the setter relies on

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of moth is taken

explanation.surface: A spider hasn't unwound, but a moth is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul splits 'uncoiled': its UN joins 'hasn't' as fodder and 'coiled' twists the lot; 'initially' takes moth's first letter and 'trapped' holds it inside. 25 is SPIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the huntsman is a large, fast hunting spider.
